root_cause.text: The function `xchk_btree_check_block_owner` in XFS scrubbing dereferences `bs->cur->bc_ops` to check the btree type after `bs->cur` may have become a dangling pointer due to aliasing with freed cursors in `bs->sc->sa.{bno,rmap}_cur`, leading to a use-after-free.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "We cannot dereference bs->cur when trying to determine if bs->cur aliases bs->sc->sa.{bno,rmap}_cur after the latter has been freed. Fix this by sampling before type before any freeing could happen." The patch moves the `xfs_btree_is_bno` and `xfs_btree_is_rmap` calls to before the points where `bs->cur` is set to `NULL` (after the `xchk_xref_is_only_owned_by` call may have freed the aliased cursors), preventing the UAF. The temporal ordering was broken when commit `ec793e690f801d` removed `xfs_btnum_t`.
